name: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Phelan-McDermid Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of deletion or mutation involving the SHANK3 gene confirmed by genetic testing
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Presence of autism spectrum disorder behaviors or diagnosis
Severe speech delay or absent speech

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of SHANK3 deletion or mutation plus presence of intellectual disability or developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on genetic testing; clinical features support but are variable.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Global developmental delay or intellectual disability

common.notes: Including insomnia and irregular sleep patterns
Includes dolichocephaly, full cheeks, and prominent ears

occasional.symptomName: Behavioral problems including anxiety and hyperactivity

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible hypothyroidism on thyroid panel
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings or delayed myelination
Renal ultrasound may reveal structural anomalies
genetic: Deletion or mutation involving SHANK3 gene on chromosome 22q13
Array comparative genomic hybridization (aCGH) or targeted sequencing confirms diagnosis
other: Neuropsychological testing confirms intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic happy demeanor and frequent laughter

redFlags: Severe global developmental delay with absent speech
Autism spectrum behaviors combined with genetic abnormalities
references: Phelan K, McDermid HE. The 22q13.3 deletion syndrome (Phelan-McDermid syndrome). Mol Syndromol. 2012;2(3-5):186-201.
Soorya L, Kolevzon A, Zweifach J, et al. Prospective investigation of autism and genotype-phenotype correlations in 22q13 deletion syndrome and SHANK3 deficiency. Mol Autism. 2013;4(1):18.

Wilson HL, Wong AC, Shaw SR, et al. Molecular characterization of the 22q13 deletion syndrome supports the role of haploinsufficiency of SHANK3/PROSAP2 in the major neurological symptoms. J Med Genet. 2003;40(8):575-584.
